The scientific work was completed before the connection failed. I recovered the proof files, executable results and the **627-file archive**, and verified that the archive is intact.

## Strongest available result

I constructed a **scheduled quantum architecture whose encoded protection improves systematically at fixed, nonzero physical noise and control ratios**, despite a retained, interacting, noisy entropy apparatus.

The central contribution is a **joint process certificate**. It derives bounds on simultaneous reset failures and damage to live quantum data from their actual coupled dynamics, then converts those bounds into the complete channel condition needed for fault tolerance. The controller and drains can retain syndrome history; they need not be restored to fresh states between cycles.

The strongest physical version uses **three modeled qubits per working wire, before error-correction and routing overhead**. It resets retired wires directly, includes finite switching ramps, and permits equal gate and cooling strengths.

This is a complete mathematical construction within an explicit open-system model. Its maintained finite-temperature dissipative ports and prescribed pulse schedule remain supplied physical resources. It does not yet establish an autonomous device, a competitive threshold, or an advantage over conventional fault tolerance equipped with independent local reset.

## 1. The physical construction

At each working-wire site, place three qubits:

| Component | Role | Noise retained in the model |
|---|---|---|
| \(D_i\) | Data, syndrome, routing or coherent-feedback wire | Bit and phase noise, control errors, residual contacts |
| \(B_i\) | Drain used during reset | Continuous loss, positive heating, contact errors |
| \(C_i\) | Part of a retained entropy-control network | Continuing noise and arbitrary retained correlations |

The layout is a slab of fixed thickness. Intended Hamiltonian terms act on one or two qubits. The operational graph has degree at most five; an enlarged graph allowing generic two-qubit faults within neighboring columns has degree at most fourteen.

\[
H_i(t)=
u_i(t)\bigl(\sigma^+_{D_i}\sigma^-_{B_i}+\mathrm{h.c.}\bigr)
+n_{B_i}F_i(C)+K_i.
\]

source_excerpts.text:
## The strongest result is a physical return mechanism with noisy controllers

I constructed a finite Hamiltonian entropy buffer whose **actual coupled dynamics** supports continued quantum protection. The model includes data faults, contact heating, finite controller response, imperfect preparation, returning excitations and the final decoded output.

The main advance in this continuation is a sufficient principle:

> **The entropy sink may retain the syndrome and its history. Protection requires that this history have sufficiently little influence on the region where continuing faults can damage the logical state.**

I earned that condition for an explicit spin-buffer model. It does not require the entire emitted field to forget, an exactly resetting recovery cycle, or an ideal correction inserted between physical steps. The complete statement protects unknown inputs entangled with arbitrary references.

This is a constructive mathematical result with executable evidence. Its constants remain too conservative to establish a competitive prototype or a scalable fault-tolerance threshold.

## 1. The physical construction

The construction retains the three-data-spin code and its exact identification
\[
\mathcal H_D\simeq \mathcal H_L\otimes\mathbb C^4.
\]
The four-dimensional syndrome factor is represented by two syndrome bits. Each becomes the endpoint of a finite XX spin chain.

For each chain, the actual Hamiltonian is
\[
H=
\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}(\omega+v_j)n_j
+\sum_{j=0}^{L-2}J_j
  \bigl(\sigma_j^+\sigma_{j+1}^-+\mathrm{h.c.}\bigr)
+\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}\chi n_j Z_{\tau_j}.
\]

Here \(j=0\) is an encoded syndrome endpoint; the other sites are physical buffer spins. Each real buffer spin has a two-state controller \(\tau_j\). Actual controller flips \(r\mathcal D[X_{\tau_j}]\) produce a field with finite correlation time:
\[
\mathbb E[Z_{\tau_j}(t)Z_{\tau_j}(0)]
=e^{-2r|t|}.
\]

The controllers are retained in the dynamics. Their effect is **not replaced by a white-noise dephaser**. Additional controller Pauli faults are allowed: their \(X/Y\) components increase the actual flip rate, while their \(Z\) component cannot affect the relevant controller-diagonal sector.

The three-component trimer data noise continues throughout. Both first real buffer spins also undergo depolarization, including heating. During operation, no buffer spin is reset or replaced.
